sentences.text: The petitioners have filed this claim petition against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Sri.P.Afroz S/o Pathan Reddy Masthan Vali, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.
02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:

On 02.04.2023 at about 03.00 p.m, in front of SVT Tyre Shop, on Madanapalle Punganur Main Road, (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 H/O Basinikonda of Madanapalle, Andhra Pradesh, when the deceased was travelling in a two-wheeler as a pillion rider, at that time one Lorry bearing No. TN-34-X-9585 came rashly and negligently and dashed against the deceased.
Due to impact the said P.Afroz fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot and petitioners have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of deadbody and last rites.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged 21 years and was working as Mechanic and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and was the only bread earner in their family and the family members depended on the income of the deceased.

Due to death of the deceased, the petitioners No.1 and 2 have lost their loving and supportive son and his love and affection and petitioner No.3 has lost her caring and supportive brother and his love and affection and put to great agony, pain, frustration and deep mental stress.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of above said Lorry by its driver and the Madanapalle Rural Police have registered a case against driver of said lorry.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Lorry
, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 did not appeared before the tribunal and hence, was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and denied alleged accident, death of deceased, age, occupation, income of deceased, dependency of the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners and contended that the alleged accident is head on collusion.
As per the Sketch the place of accident is shown on the middle of the road and as per IMV report both vehicles sustained damages on the front portion.
Both the rider and pillion rider were not wearing helmet, they sustained head injuries.

The rider of Motor Cycle riding in rash and negligent manner by talking with pillion rider and dashed to the lorry and there is no fault or rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of lorry and hence, contributory negligence is more on the part of both rider and pillion rider of Motor Cycle.

The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties such as owner and insurer of the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 unregistered Motor Cycle and denied existence of policy of insurance in respect of offending lorry and the liability

sentences.text: The driver of the offending lorry did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident and valid and effective Permit and FC as on the date of accident and hence there is violation of policy conditions and hence this respondent is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 and not liable to pay compensation.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.

05. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES
01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.P.Afroz S/o Pathan Reddy Masthan Vali?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.P.Afroz S/o Pathan Reddy Masthan Vali died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 02.04.2023 at about 03.00 p.m, in front of SVT Tyre Shop, near Kanumalo Gangamma Temple, Madanapalle Mandal, on Madanapalle (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 Punganur Main Road, Basinikonda Hobli, Annamayya District, Andhra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Lorry bearing registration No.TN-34-X-9585 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04. What order or award?
06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.3 is examined as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14 and closed their side evidence.
Despite sufficient opportunity has been given, the respondent No.1 did not lead evidence and hence respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.1 and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:

sentences.text: 3 09. Issues No.1 and 2:- Since these two issues are interconnected to each other and in order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record, these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
10. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.3 is examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments.
Though she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.
11. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 14 documents as Ex.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Madanapalle Rural Police against driver of offending Lorry for his rash and negligent driving and causing death of deceased.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint lodged against driver of offending Lorry.

Ex.P.3 is copy of Post mortem report of deceased P.Afroz wherein it is stated that deceased died in road traffic accident and he was died due to hemorrhage and shock due to head injury sustained due to road traffic accident.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Inquest (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 report of deceased P.Afroz.
Ex.P.5 is Accident information report.
Ex.P.6 is copy of IMV report which indicates involvement of offending lorry in the accident.
Ex.P.7 is copy of hand Sketch map which shows that negligence is on the part of the driver of the offending lorry.

Ex.P.8 is copy of Charge sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending Lorry and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and causing accident and causing death of deceased.
Ex.P.9 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1.
Ex.P.10 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.2.
Ex.P.11 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.3.
Ex.P.12 is copy of Aadhaar card of deceased.
Ex.P.13 is copy of Rice card and Ex.P.14 is copy of Death certificate of deceased who died on road traffic accident and was died on 02.04.2023.

12. On going through the oral and documentary evidence adduced and produced by the petitioners,
it clearly establishes that deceased P.Afroz was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 02.04.2023 at about 03.00 p.m, in front of SVT Tyre Shop, on Madanapalle Punganur Main Road,
H/O Basinikonda of Madanapalle, Andhra Pradesh, due to rash and (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 negligent act of driving of Lorry bearing No. TN-34-X-9585, by its driver.
Further as per Ex.

P.9 to 12 Aadhaar cards and Ex.P.13 Rice card, which indicates that petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the father and petitioner No.3 is the sister of deceased and they are legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased
. Accordingly, these Issues No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased P.Afroz, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

PW.1 who is the sister of the deceased has stated that prior to accident her brother was aged about 21 years and was working as Mechanic and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners have lost their son and brother, undergone great mental shock, agony, discomfort and financial loss.
They have also spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of deadbody and last rites.

sentences.text: It is the duty of the petitioner to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The petitioners have not produced any school records such as birth certificate or SSLC marks card for the proof of age of (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 the deceased.
But they have produced Ex.P.12 the copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased.

Though it is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the said document the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 29.09.2002 and the alleged accident occurred on 02.04.2023

. Hence, considering the Post mortem report, Police records and medical records and Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card of deceased, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 21 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is 18 and the same is considered.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. So far as avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not produced any evidence or documents.

Since there is no proof of documents regarding avocation and income of the deceased, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru and as per norms for the year 2023 the notional income is Rs.16,000/- p.m and hence, this tribunal has assessed the notional (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
16.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The deceased has left behind 3 dependents.

In this regard the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in a decision reported in 2020 SCC ONLINE SC 28 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Birender, it has been held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased are entitled to make an application for compensation in view of Sec.166 (1)(c) of the Act.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Birender
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It has further been held that, even major married and earning sons of the deceased being the legal representatives have right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representatives was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claims towards conventional heads only".
17.

In the instant case, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 being the mother, petitioner No.2 being the father and petitioner No.3 being the sister of deceased are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

It is evident that the deceased in the present case was a bachelor and hence 1/2 of the income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
18.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi &
Others case in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.

In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects of the deceased is taking into consideration.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. Since the deceased was aged about 21 years at the time of the accident, 40% of the income is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospectus, which would result in the Pathan Reddibee vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120676829/

entities.text: Pathan Reddibee vs National Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was a bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and then his monthly income would be Rs.11,200/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.11,200/-.
As the deceased was aged 21 years, a multiplier of 18 would have to be applied.
Consequently the petitioners (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 would be entitled for a sum of Rs.24,19,200/- (Rs.11,200 x 12 x 18) towards loss of dependency.

20. The claimants No.1 and 2 being the parents of the deceased would be entitled for Rs.48,000/-
each towards loss of filial consortium.
The claimant No.3 being the sister of the deceased would be entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/2 of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency (After 24,19,200-00 deducting  of the income towards personal and living expenses)
2. Loss of filial consortium 96,000-00 3. Loss of estate 18,000-00 4.
Funeral expenses and 18,000-00 transportation of dead (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 body 5. Loss of love and affection 40,000-00

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,91,200/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
22. In this case the respondent No.1 has taken several defences, but not lead any evidence.
The respondent No.2 is placed exparte.

The respondent No.1 Insurance Company in its written statement has denied the issuance of insurance policy, but not contested the matter and even Police have not filed Charge sheet against owner for driving the lorry without insurance and as per the averments made in the petition the policy No.651900312210000911 valid from 30.05.2022 to 29.05.2023.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending lorry was valid and is in force.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay compensation amount of Rs.25,91,200/- with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, this Issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER

The claim petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act,
1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,91,200/- (Rupees Twenty five lakhs ninety one thousand and two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, petitioners No.1 and 2 being the parents of the deceased and petitioner No.3 being the sister of the deceased were apportioned the compensation (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 equally in the ratio of 50:30:20, in the award amount together with interest.

The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award amount through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the duty of the petitioner to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased.
Though it is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the said document the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 29.09.2002 and the alleged accident occurred on 02.04.2023
. Hence, considering the Post mortem report, Police records and medical records and Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card of deceased, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 21 years.
Since there is no proof of documents regarding avocation and income of the deceased, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru and as per norms for the year 2023 the notional income is Rs.16,000/- p.m and hence, this tribunal has assessed the notional (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
16.
In the instant case, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 being the mother, petitioner No.2 being the father and petitioner No.3 being the sister of deceased are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.
It is evident that the deceased in the present case was a bachelor and hence 1/2 of the income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
18.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi &
Others case in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.
19. Since the deceased was aged about 21 years at the time of the accident, 40% of the income is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospectus, which would result in the Pathan Reddibee vs National Ins Co Ltd on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120676829/
Since the deceased was a bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and then his monthly income would be Rs.11,200/-.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.4024/2023 respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay compensation amount of Rs.25,91,200/- with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
